title: Finite equations of finite free sheaf maps shrink from a stalk
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a finite indexing type, and $A_i,B_i$ sheaves of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Each $A_i$ and $B_i$ is zero or isomorphic to a finite free sheaf [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Let $y\in U\subseteq Y$ with $U$ open. Given maps $f_i,g_i:R_U A_i\to R_U B_i$, where $R_U$ is open restriction, suppose $S_U(f_i)=S_U(g_i)$, where $S_U$ is module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] along $U.\mathrm{fromSpecStalkOfMem}(y)$. Then there are an open $V\subseteq U$ containing $y$ and its inclusion $j:V\to U$ such that $R_j(f_i)=R_j(g_i)$ for all $i$. No complexes, differentials, or comparisons of stalk pullbacks are involved.

source.place: lem-pc-finite-free-stalk-degreewise-shrink, steps 1 and 2: finite matrices of commutativity defects, zero-germ shrinking

proof.text: Induct over a finite set of indices. For the empty family use U. For the insertion of i let V be the neighbourhood supplied by the induction hypothesis. If A_i or B_i is zero, restriction preserves zero objects (Functor.map_isZero) and maps out of or into a zero object are unique (IsZero.eq_of_src, IsZero.eq_of_tgt); retain V.

In the remaining case A_i has a finite free isomorphism. Map it by restrictFunctor U.ι to obtain the source isomorphism required by lem-pc-finite-free-stalk-map-eq-shrink. Apply that lemma to f_i,g_i on U with additional neighbourhood V. This yields W≤V containing y, with their direct restrictions from U equal.

Previously obtained equalities on V persist on W. The natural isomorphism restrictFunctorCongr composed with restrictFunctorComp identifies restriction along homOfLE (W≤U) with the composition of the two restrictions; apply its naturality and cancel its isomorphism component. Applying the restriction functor to the old equality gives the new one. This closes the induction; use the full finite set of indices.

proof_origin.place: Finite germ equality argument, using the existing finite-free-source local map equality lemma and finite-set induction. Formalized by C2; no matrix construction is required.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_shrink_finite_free_map_eq
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (A B : ι → Y.Modules)
    (hA : ∀ i, IsZero (A i) ∨ ∃ s : ℕ, Nonempty
      (A i ≅ SheafOfModules.free (R := Y.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin s))))
    (hB : ∀ i, IsZero (B i) ∨ ∃ s : ℕ, Nonempty
      (B i ≅ SheafOfModules.free (R := Y.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin s))))
    (y : Y) (U : Y.Opens) (hyU : y ∈ U)
    (f g : ∀ i, (restrictFunctor U.ι).obj (A i) ⟶
      (restrictFunctor U.ι).obj (B i))
    (h : ∀ i, (Modules.pullback (U.fromSpecStalkOfMem y hyU)).map (f i) =
      (Modules.pullback (U.fromSpecStalkOfMem y hyU)).map (g i)) :
    ∃ (V : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ V) (hVU : V ≤ U),
      ∀ i, (restrictFunctor (Y.homOfLE hVU)).map (f i) =
        (restrictFunctor (Y.homOfLE hVU)).map (g i)
